_doc: Locale pack for funnel-localize. Language facts drive translation; market facts drive code (shared/locales.ts mirrors the market half). Decisions marked `decide` are proposals for the operator at Gate G2.

buyerGender.decide: The funnel's buyers are women (VOC). French must agree adjectives with her: « prête », « sûre ». Proposed: feminine by default.

market.legal: EU consumer law + French Code de la consommation; see legal.md

prices._note: Same numbers as the US funnel, in euros, incl. VAT (TTC). Written « 35 € » / « 12,77 € » (comma decimals, space before €).
prices.decide: Mirror the US numbers 1:1 in EUR (proposed), or set a French table.

priceRule: Three shapes in the English. (1) '${x}': the $ is a literal sign and {x} is a bare number → write '{x} €' (number, space, €). (2) '{price}', '{priceLabel}': the placeholder already holds the full amount with its currency → never add € or $ next to it. (3) a written amount like '$30' → '30 €' (same number). No '$' may remain in the French. The code formats the numbers fr-FR (comma decimals) and the checker makes the space before € non-breaking.

prompts._doc: The wording the pipeline's prompts need in THIS language (scripts/l10n/prompts.mts reads it). Everything else in the prompts is shared by every language. The model-facing JSON field for the translation is the language code before the dash (fr).
prompts.writer: You write it as a native French copywriter would write it from scratch: natural, spoken, warm French that does not read as translated.
prompts.buyer: The buyer is a woman in France, usually 45+.
prompts.localeFlag: not France French (Québec, Belgian), US formats, a "$" sign
prompts.intended: prices in euros ("35 €") where the English has dollars; "dear" left out on most lines (« ma chère » only at warm moments, at most once a message); "vous" everywhere; the house terms below; English names (Evelyn Cross, The Seer Within) kept; an English promise of an outcome ("That I promise you", "it ends now") softened on purpose for French consumer law; a short label in lower case where it completes a sentence the page builds (« Evelyn Cross est » + « en ligne »).
prompts.rejectExamples: "tu", a proverb, a dollar sign, a literal "dear" on every line, or it undoes the glossary

checks._doc: Mechanical checks that depend on the language or market (scripts/l10n/check.mts).

currencyLeft.detail: a '$' is left in the French (see pack.json priceRule)

review._doc: Labels for the operator's review page (scripts/l10n/review-page.mts). risk = the market's rule behind each risk tag the translator sets (legal.md).

danger.title: Danger if she doesn't buy
danger.rule: Banned outright when inaccurate (Code de la consommation L121-4 12°); exploiting distress can make it an aggressive practice (L121-6, L121-7). Needs rewriting, not just a label.

urgency.title: Time or places limited
urgency.rule: False scarcity is banned outright (L121-4 7°). Keep only limits that are true.

claim.title: Claims that need proof
claim.rule: Customer counts, testimonials (fake reviews: L121-4 28°), Evelyn's lineage, promised results (L121-2).

ai-identity.title: Evelyn presented as a person
ai-identity.rule: EU AI Act Art. 50(1): a person chatting with an AI must be told, unless it is obvious.

consent.title: Consent, refunds, withdrawal
consent.rule: E-mail and pixel consent (CNIL); the 14-day withdrawal right and the refund promise must be described separately.
